Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J24/J24nB138.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen. Yunmen Wenyan owns the retained supply: a monk took leave of Shishuang Qingzhu — by boat or by land? — meet a boat, take the boat; meet land, take the land — I say the halfway point is rather hard — and the monk had no words; the master supplied: thirty years on, this saying will travel everywhere — and again: one line at parting, unforgotten for a whole aeon.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (D/D48/D48n8939.xml). Recorded Sayings of Ancient Venerable Masters. Baiyun Shouduan owns the retained dare: Mahakasyapa's eyes, Anguilimala's stripes, Mudgalyana's feet crossing the pit, Mahakasyapa the elder dancing to the zither, Pilingkajie cursing the river spirit, Kalingudayin buried in dung — each has its warrant in the teaching; and at the gate of the founder: nine years facing the wall, Bimo's staff, Heshan's drum, Shigong's bow, Xuefeng's ball, the National Master's water bowl, Guizong dragging stone, Deshan's staff at the door, Linji's shout at the door, Wuye's 'give up deluded thinking' — say, what is this? is there in the throng one long-trained worthy who walks crosswise under heaven with an eye above the crown of his head? come out and stand witness for Baiyun, and give this life one free breath — anyone? anyone? if not — thirty years on, this saying will travel — and how, in the end? the summer's fire-clouds return to the blue cave; clear autumn's perilous dew drips on the golden plate.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2004.xml). Wansong's Commentary and Chanting on Tiantong Jue's Verse-Comments on the Ancients: Record of the Congrong Hermitage. Wansong Xingxiu owns the retained gloss: the Mao ode 'Qiyu' praises the Duke of Wu — a man of letters who could still hear remonstrance, guarding himself by ritual, hence rising to minister at Zhou; cut bone, file ivory, carve jade, grind stone — Deshan's Xuefeng won his final word from Yantou, and to this day this saying travels: the power of cutting and grinding, of turning and changing; Xuefeng is the staff that turns into a dragon, that monk the shuttle still coiled in its cocoon; Yantou pointed it out and to this day no one knows — hence 'dying on the same branch' has few.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1412.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Gulin Qingmao. Gulin Qingmao owns the retained verdict: Zhuyu held up a peg of bamboo in the hall — can anyone drive a peg into empty space? — elder Lingxu came out: empty space is the peg — Zhuyu struck him; do not strike me in error — and Zhuyu let it rest; Xuedou's verdict: to make this saying travel, you must finish the strikes and chase him out; the master's own: to make this saying travel, you must drive the peg into empty space — and if some fellow comes out and says 'empty space is the peg,' how do you answer? a horse run on ice-edges, a body turned on the sword-blade — that is my everyday use; let it pass, and where would this crew of sleepers grope? — and he drove them all out with a flurry of the staff.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB294.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liangting Ting of Yunxi. Liangting Jingting owns the retained tea-talk: the clouds and the moon are the same, the streams and the hills each differ — back then Jiashan and Luopu cut off the tongue, this saying traveled, and so this day came to be; today the stream and moon are wholly the same, the clouds and hills not different: brows level, nose straight, the swan white, the crow black; come from Tiantai heading to Jingshan, all together walk into Xixi, by the misty-water road enter the gate of the towered pavilion, and pass the river islet without escape — the whale swallows the sea and bares the coral; let Jiashan's Boatman, Nanyue and Qingyuan, all the old augers from the beginning, be drawn by one rope to that side — a fair share of freedom and ease.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB454.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Pinjixiang. Pinjixiang Zhixiang owns the retained stamp: asked — a lifespan beyond dust-aeons, please point it out — the winter plum on the ridge is just baring its jade; then the whole great earth shares the moistening — Muzhou only carries the board; Nanquan is used to selling himself; heaven and earth one root — there really is the way! — and the master: thirty years on, this saying will travel — then, to the hall: the affair under the founders demands you sweat out a whole white sweat before you know the descending pure wind; though Yangshan said it cannot be said, he only watched heaven tip in the southeast and never saw earth notch in the northwest; and even one who could say it is not allowed to sit with Chen of Muzhou and old teacher Wang — to know the meaning of a lifespan beyond dust-aeons, wait straight until thirty years on, when someone will raise it of himself.

Senses.Explanation: This saying will travel: a supplied answer, a dare to the silent hall, a price put on a word thirty years out. Yunmen Wenyan, over a case already closed in silence: a monk leaving Shishuang Qingzhu — by boat or by land? — meet a boat, take the boat; meet land, take the land — I say the halfway point is rather hard — no words; and the master supplied: thirty years on, this saying will travel — one line at parting, unforgotten for a whole aeon. Baiyun Shouduan, after the founders' roll-call — the wall-facing nine years, the staff, the drum, the bow, the ball, the water bowl, the dragged stone, the shout at the door — say, what is this? is there one who walks crosswise under heaven with an eye above his crown? come out and stand witness for Baiyun; anyone? anyone? if not — thirty years on, this saying will travel. Wansong Xingxiu, glossing the cutting-polishing ode: Deshan's Xuefeng won his final word from Yantou, and to this day this saying travels — the power of cutting and grinding; Xuefeng is the staff that turns into a dragon, that monk the shuttle still coiled; Yantou pointed it out and no one to this day knows. Gulin Qingmao, over the peg in empty space: Zhuyu held up the bamboo peg; elder Lingxu said empty space is the peg and took the strike; Xuedou's verdict — finish the strikes and chase him out; the master's own — to make this saying travel, drive the peg into empty space; and if someone says 'empty space is the peg,' how do you answer? — a horse on the ice-edges, a body turned on the sword-blade; let it pass, and where would the sleepers grope? Nanyuan Huiyong, carried in Sanfeng's genealogy: a monk from Xiangzhou come specially to bow — you have just missed the old man of Baoying, he is not in — a shout; I told you he is not in — another shout, and the staff; the monk bowed: this staff was by rights yours to strike me — I strike you with it instead — this saying must travel — blind man, off to the hall! Liangting Jingting, over tea: the clouds and the moon are the same, the streams and hills each differ — back then Jiashan and Luopu cut off the tongue, this saying traveled, and so this day came to be; today brows level, nose straight, the swan white, the crow black — and let all the old augers from Jiashan's Boatman to Nanyue and Qingyuan be drawn by one rope to that side. Pinjixiang Zhixiang, on the heaven-earth-one-root exchange: a lifespan beyond dust-aeons — the winter plum just baring its jade; the whole earth shares the moistening — Muzhou only carries the board, Nanquan is used to selling himself — heaven and earth one root, there really is the way! — and the master: thirty years on, this saying will travel — and it demands a whole white sweat of you; even one who could say it is not allowed to sit with Chen of Muzhou and old teacher Wang; wait thirty years, and someone will raise it of himself.
